about.title: Holly has tight village lots and **lakeside acreage.**
body: A Holly address can mean the village, the township around it or even Rose Township to the south. The Village of Holly runs its own public works, and its streets are older and closer together, with alleys and a few dirt roads that the village plows itself. Past the village line is the outer township, where most roads are gravel and the Road Commission for Oakland County does the plowing.

Out in the township, many lawns run down to a lake or a wetland edge, back up to woods or roll over hills. The ground changes with them: heavier soil on much of the higher ground, sand across a good share of the township and muck in the low spots and bogs.
A lawn on the sandy stretches browns out first in a dry July, and a bed dug near a wetland edge stays wet into June. We plan the work around which of those your yard has.

points.title: Gravel roads and a late county plow
points.body: Most outer township roads are gravel, and the road commission puts sand on them because salt does little on gravel. Subdivision streets get plowed after the main roads, so a driveway that is already clear is the part you can count on.

points.title: Older, tighter village lots
points.body: Inside the village, homes sit closer together, with walks, curbs and alleys around them. That is trimmer and edger work, and the clippings have to end up on the lawn, not on the neighbor's drive.

points.title: Oak leaves come down late
points.body: The township's plan says its high ground grew up in oak woods, and MSU Extension notes many oaks hold their dead leaves into winter. Leaves keep falling after a yard looks finished, so a wooded lot often needs a late fall visit.

points.title: Young yards on rolling ground
points.body: Nearly 40% of township homes went up between 2000 and 2010. Many of those yards are still young: graded slopes, builder foundation shrubs that have outgrown the windows, and beds that were never really finished.

points.title: No township truck for leaves
points.body: The township runs no garbage collection, and its fall cleanup day turns away leaves. In the village they go out in paper bags or marked containers through November 30, and the village does not allow leaves or brush to be burned.

logistics.title: Village or township, the visit runs the same way.
body: Rob answers the phone and the texts. Tell him where the property is and what you want done, and he will set a time to come out, walk it with you and suggest what it needs. Then you get a price, and the work goes on the calendar.

Lake lots and long wooded drives are worth a few extra notes at that first visit: a gate code, a dog, a shared drive, a soft spot near the shoreline. Our trucks and trailers are full size, so we look at where they can park and turn before the first job instead of on the day of it.

We work in Holly from our shop on Embury Road in Grand Blanc, about 20 minutes away. Call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040), [text Rob](sms:+18109903040) or send the [estimate form](/get-an-estimate/).

faq.q: Do you do lawn care and landscaping in Holly, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes works in the Village of Holly and across Holly Township from our shop in Grand Blanc. We do [weekly lawn mowing](/lawn-mowing-holly-mi/), [spring cleanups](/spring-cleanup-holly-mi/), [fall leaf removal](/leaf-removal-holly-mi/), [mulch and bed work](/mulch-installation-holly-mi/), [landscaping](/landscaping-holly-mi/) and [snow removal](/snow-removal-holly-mi/). Overgrown bushes and small trees, yes; big trees, no.

faq.q: Who plows the road in front of my house?
faq.a: It depends on which side of the village line you live on. Inside the village, its public works department plows the streets, alleys and dirt roads. Out in the township, the Road Commission for Oakland County plows, and it works main roads first and subdivision streets last. Either way, the end of your driveway is yours, and that is the part we clear.

faq.q: Can I burn leaves in Holly?
faq.a: Not in the village. The fire department's burn permit rules list leaves and brush among the things that cannot be burned. In the outer township, all open burning needs a permit from the North Oakland County Fire Authority under the township ordinance. Rules change, so check with them first, or have a [fall cleanup](/leaf-removal-holly-mi/) haul the leaves away.

faq.q: Is the soil sandy around Holly?
faq.a: In places. The township's master plan describes heavier soil under the village and most built up areas, sand across a good share of the township and muck near the lakes and wetlands. Sandy soil holds less water than loam, MSU Extension notes, so those lawns brown out sooner in a dry spell.

faq.q: When is overnight parking banned on village streets in winter?
faq.a: The village snow ordinance, as last published, bans parking on village streets from 3 to 7 AM between December 1 and March 30, so the plows can get through. Check with the village office for the current wording. It also means more cars in driveways overnight, so tell us where yours usually sit.
